In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pseudomonas aceA gene is required for the growth on acetate, citrate, citronell, n-octane, leucine and isocitrate.
the aceA (isocitrate lyases) genes in the PAO1 and PAO1R strains encode an enzyme involved in the assimilative pathways of acetate, leucine, acyclic monotrepenes, and n-octanol.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ICL is an important metabolic enzyme that is involved in the catabolism of a wide variety of substrates in P. aeruginosa.
the ICL enzyme of P. aeruginosa is involved in the utilization of acetate, citrate, citronellols, and leuine, and is repressed by glucose.
ICL plays a key role in the utilization of acetate and leucine as carbon and nitrogen sources, and that the ICL gene is a potential target for the design of novel antibiotics against P. aeruginosa.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ICL enzyme of P. aeruginosa is not involved in the assimilatory pathways of the citrate cycle, but in an alternative metabolic pathway, which is induced by growth on acetate, leucine, or acyclic monoterpones.
ICL is a new target for the design of antimicrobials against P. aeruginosa, which is a major pathogen of humans and animals.
ICL is required for the assimilation of leucine, acyclic monotrepenes, alkanols and acetate in P. aeruginosa.
